t: #3889 Mirror Frequency Distance — Frequency Map Over Mirror Pairs
o: Mirror each letter (a<->z, b<->y, ...) and digit (0<->9, 1<->8, ...). For each unordered pair {c, m(c)}, add |freq(c) - freq(m)|. Counting each pair once is easiest by iterating characters c and only processing those with c < m(c) (note no character is its own mirror since alphabets have even sizes). Example 'ab1z9': pairs (a,z) diff 0, (b,y) diff 1, (1,8) diff 1, (9,0) diff 1 -> 3.
k: Mirror maps letters via chr(ord('z') - (ord(c) - ord('a'))) and digits via str(9 - d).
Iterate present characters and count a pair only when c < mirror(c) to avoid double counting.

a.n: Approach 1: Frequency counter with canonical pair orientation
a.i: Tally frequencies in one pass, then for each present character whose mirror is lexicographically greater, add the absolute frequency difference against the mirror's frequency (default 0).
s: Build a frequency map of s.
Define the mirror function for letters and digits.
For each character c in the map with c < mirror(c), add |freq(c) - freq(mirror(c))|.
a.t: O(|s| + 36) — one pass to count, constant work over the 36 possible characters.

w: Simple but easy to fumble: the classic bug is counting both orientations of each pair (doubling the answer) — the c < m(c) guard fixes it. Another pitfall is mixing letter and digit mirrors. Edge cases: strings where every character appears with its mirror equally often return 0. Follow-up: mirror defined by reversing only within case groups, or weighted differences.
